title: Q: Equal-mass aluminium and copper spheres — which cools faster?
notes: **Setup:** aluminium (c = 900 J/kg·K) and copper (c = 390 J/kg·K) spheres of equal mass are heated to the same temperature and cooled under identical conditions
Identical conditions ⇒ same rate of heat loss (dH/dt) for both spheres at a given instant, by Newton's Law of Cooling
But −dH/dt = mc·(dθ/dt), so dθ/dt = (dH/dt)/(mc) — for the same dH/dt, a smaller c gives a larger dθ/dt
**Answer: Copper (lower c) cools faster** — its temperature falls more quickly even though it isn't losing heat energy any faster than the aluminium sphere

Equal masses of aluminium and copper, cooling in the same way, can lose heat at the same rate at the same temperature. The copper has the smaller specific heat, so the same heat loss drops its temperature faster. Losing heat faster is not the same statement as cooling faster.

exercises.question: Both spheres have mass 0.20 kg. c_Al = 900 and c_Cu = 390, in J/kg K. At an instant both lose heat at 20 W. Find each dθ/dt.
steps: For aluminium, 20 = 0.20 × 900 × rate, so the rate is 20/180 = 0.11 K/s.
For copper, 20 = 0.20 × 390 × rate, so the rate is 20/78 = 0.26 K/s.
The heat-loss rate was the same by the setup.
exercises.answer: Aluminium about 0.11 K/s. Copper about 0.26 K/s. Copper cools faster.

summary: Equal heat-loss rates do not mean equal cooling rates. With c = 900 and 390, the same 20 W drops the copper's temperature faster, about 0.26 K/s against 0.11 K/s for the aluminium.
